dedupeText: vintage country western album cover cowboy hat western slab serif 1960s photography warm lighting album art text is anchored to the top left corner balancing the subject s face on the right the dark cowboy hat creates a large solid shape that frames the upper half of the image warm reddish orange lighting on the face contrasts with the dark cool toned background the tracklist is centered beneath the main title in a smaller lighter weight font take a moody warm toned portrait of a western figure frame it to the right and anchor heavy slab serif typography in the top left negative space

retrievalProfile.description: A classic 1960s country music aesthetic featuring a close-up portrait of a man in a cowboy hat with heavy slab-serif typography and a warm, moody color palette.

recipe.visualDefinition: A square composition dominated by a warm-toned, slightly low-angle portrait of a man wearing a dark cowboy hat, with text clustered in the upper left corner using heavy, decorative slab-serif fonts.
coreVisualRelationships: Text is anchored to the top-left corner, balancing the subject's face on the right.
The dark cowboy hat creates a large, solid shape that frames the upper half of the image.
Warm, reddish-orange lighting on the face contrasts with the dark, cool-toned background.
The tracklist is centered beneath the main title in a smaller, lighter weight font.
coreInvariants: Heavy slab-serif display type for the primary name.
Subject wearing a wide-brimmed cowboy hat.

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: The subject is positioned in the lower right quadrant, scaled to a medium close-up.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The subject's face, specifically the eyes, serves as the primary focal point.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: Eyes start at the bold title in the top left, move down through the tracklist, and settle on the subject's face.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: The dark area of the hat and the background provide significant negative space for text placement.

colorSystem.dominantColorRole: Deep browns and blacks in the hat and background.
colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Warm peach and orange skin tones.
colorSystem.accentColorRole: Creamy white and golden yellow for the typography.
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: Low saturation overall with high value contrast between the skin and the dark hat.

letterConstructionRules: Extremely thick horizontal and vertical strokes.
Internal decorative notches or spurs on the mid-points of vertical strokes.
characterSpecificRedesigns: The 'M' and 'N' feature deep, sharp crotches.
The 'S' has heavy, horizontal slab terminals.
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: A heavy, decorative slab serif for the name paired with a simpler, smaller slab serif for the title and tracklist.

candidateDirections.reason: Matches the heavy, western slab-serif aesthetic with decorative spurs.
Provides the necessary weight and slab-serif structure.

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a portrait of a man with 1960s hair wearing a dark brown cowboy hat and a leather jacket. Use warm, low-key lighting with a reddish-orange glow on the face. The background should be dark and slightly out of focus. Leave the top-left quadrant empty for text.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Add the artist name in a heavy, cream-colored western slab-serif font in the top left. Below it, add the album title in a smaller, golden-yellow slab-serif font. Below that, add a list of song titles in a small, light-weight cream font, all left-aligned.

verificationChecks: Is the main text a heavy slab-serif?
Is the subject wearing a cowboy hat?
Is the lighting warm and moody?
Is the text left-aligned in the top-left corner?

adjustableVariables: Intensity of the warm lighting glow
Exact font weight of the tracklist

avoid: Overly bright or cool color palettes

postGenerationChecks: Check that the slab-serifs have the characteristic 'western' spurs.
Ensure the color palette remains in the warm brown/orange/cream range.
Verify the text does not overlap the subject's face.
Confirm the overall square aspect ratio typical of vinyl covers.
recipe.reuseFormula: Take a moody, warm-toned portrait of a western figure, frame it to the right, and anchor heavy slab-serif typography in the top-left negative space.
